Treemap marker objects

Source: R/zz-gen-treemap.R
go_treemap_marker.Rd

The object for the marker of a treemap trace (go_treemap()). go_treemap_marker() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_treemap_marker(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  autocolorscale = NULL,
  cauto = NULL,
  cmax = NULL,
  cmid = NULL,
  cmin = NULL,
  coloraxis = NULL,
  colorbar = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  colorscale = NULL,
  cornerradius = NULL,
  depthfade = NULL,
  line = NULL,
  pad = NULL,
  pattern = NULL,
  reversescale = NULL,
  showscale = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

autocolorscale

Determines whether the colorscale is a default palette (`autocolorscale: true`) or the palette determined by `marker.colorscale`. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. In case `colorscale` is unspecified or `autocolorscale` is true, the default palette will be chosen according to whether numbers in the `color` array are all positive, all negative or mixed. Logical.

cauto

Determines whether or not the color domain is computed with respect to the input data (here colors) or the bounds set in `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. Defaults to `false` when `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax` are set by the user. Logical.

cmax

Sets the upper bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as colors and if set, `marker.cmin` must be set as well. Number.

cmid

Sets the mid-point of the color domain by scaling `marker.cmin` and/or `marker.cmax` to be equidistant to this point. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as colors. Has no effect when `marker.cauto` is `false`. Number.

cmin

Sets the lower bound of the color domain. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. Value should have the same units as colors and if set, `marker.cmax` must be set as well. Number.

coloraxis

Sets a reference to a shared color axis. References to these shared color axes are "coloraxis", "coloraxis2", "coloraxis3", etc. Settings for these shared color axes are set in the layout, under `layout.coloraxis`, `layout.coloraxis2`, etc. Note that multiple color scales can be linked to the same color axis. Subplot id: "coloraxis", "coloraxis2", "coloraxis3", ....

colorbar

A go_colorbar() object or named list, with properties bgcolor, bordercolor, borderwidth, dtick, exponentformat, labelalias, len, lenmode, minexponent, nticks, orientation, outlinecolor and 34 more (see go_colorbar()).

colors

Sets the color of each sector of this trace. If not specified, the default trace color set is used to pick the sector colors. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

colorscale

Sets the colorscale. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. The colorscale must be an array containing arrays mapping a normalized value to an rgb, rgba, hex, hsl, hsla, hwb, or named color string. At minimum, a mapping for the lowest (0) and highest (1) values are required. For example, `[[0, 'rgb(0,0,255)'], [1, 'rgb(255,0,0)']]`. To control the bounds of the colorscale in color space, use `marker.cmin` and `marker.cmax`. Alternatively, `colorscale` may be a palette name string of the following list: Blackbody,Bluered,Blues,Cividis,Earth,Electric,Greens,Greys,Hot,Jet,Picnic,Portland,Rainbow,RdBu,Reds,Viridis,YlGnBu,YlOrRd. Colorscale: a vector of colors, a two-column data.frame of (value, color), or the name of a sequential, diverging or cyclical scale in px_colors() (append "_r" to reverse).

cornerradius

Sets the maximum rounding of corners (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

depthfade

Determines if the sector colors are faded towards the background from the leaves up to the headers. This option is unavailable when a `colorscale` is present, defaults to false when `marker.colors` is set, but otherwise defaults to true. When set to "reversed", the fading direction is inverted, that is the top elements within hierarchy are drawn with fully saturated colors while the leaves are faded towards the background color. One of "reversed", TRUE, FALSE.

line

A go_treemap_marker_line() object or named list, with properties color and width (see go_treemap_marker_line()).

pad

A go_treemap_marker_pad() object or named list, with properties b, l, r and t (see go_treemap_marker_pad()).

pattern

Sets the pattern within the marker. A go_pattern() object or named list, with properties bgcolor, fgcolor, fgopacity, fillmode, path, shape, size and solidity (see go_pattern()).

reversescale

Reverses the color mapping if true. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. If true, `marker.cmin` will correspond to the last color in the array and `marker.cmax` will correspond to the first color. Logical.

showscale

Determines whether or not a colorbar is displayed for this trace. Has an effect only if colors is set to a numerical array. Logical.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_treemap_marker object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

cyl <- table(paste(mtcars$cyl, "cylinders"))
d <- data.frame(
  labels = c("all cars", names(cyl)),
  parents = c("", rep("all cars", length(cyl))),
  values = c(0, as.vector(cyl))
)
d |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_treemap(
    labels = ~labels,
    parents = ~parents,
    values = ~values,
    marker = go_treemap_marker(colors = c("red", "blue"))
  )
